text:
Overall quality: **6/10**. It is small, readable, and the included tests pass, but I would not ship it as-is for production accounting because the data model can silently corrupt real Slurm histories.

Verification run: `python -m pytest -q` passed 61 tests. In-memory AST parse passed. Bytecode compile to repo-local `__pycache__` is blocked because `/work` is mounted read-only for cache writes.

**Issues**

| Severity | File | Lines | Description |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| high | [jobwatch/db.py](/work/jobwatch/db.py:14) | 14-25 | `job_id` is the sole primary key, so duplicate/requeued/federated/resized/accounting-reset Slurm records are collapsed into one row; Slurm documents that duplicate records can occur and are distinguishable by submit time or SLUID fields.  |
| high | [jobwatch/db.py](/work/jobwatch/db.py:31) | 31-41, 70-100 | All terminal states have equal rank, so ingest order can overwrite a newer terminal record with an older terminal record for the same `job_id`. |
| medium | [jobwatch/reports.py](/work/jobwatch/reports.py:16) | 16, 78-105 | Failure reports only count `FAILED`, `TIMEOUT`, `OUT_OF_MEMORY`, and `OOM`, omitting Slurm failure-like terminal states such as `BOOT_FAIL`, `DEADLINE`, `NODE_FAIL`, and `PREEMPTED`. ([slurm.schedmd.com](https://slurm.schedmd.com/job_state_codes.html)) |
| medium | [jobwatch/parser.py](/work/jobwatch/parser.py:37) | 37, 78-89 | Elapsed parsing is narrower than Slurm’s documented elapsed-time shape and rejects some valid accounting time variants.  |
| medium | [jobwatch/db.py](/work/jobwatch/db.py:13) | 13-27, 52-58 | Schema initialization has no version table or migrations, so future schema changes will fail or misbehave against existing databases. |
| medium | [jobwatch/parser.py](/work/jobwatch/parser.py:137) | 137-164 | Row validation allows empty `User`/`Partition` and negative `AllocCPUS`, producing bad report groups or negative usage. |
| low | [jobwatch/parser.py](/work/jobwatch/parser.py:178) | 178-186 | Header handling requires one exact column order and raw `line.split("|")`, making the importer brittle to otherwise valid `sacct --format` variations. |
| low | [jobwatch/cli.py](/work/jobwatch/cli.py:121) | 121-143, 172-180 | Report/read commands call `db.connect`, which silently creates a new empty database for a typo path instead of warning that no existing DB was found. |
| low | [pyproject.toml](/work/pyproject.toml:13) | 13-14 | Development tooling only declares pytest; there is no lint/type/static check configured for the cleanup pass. |

Estimated rewrite/significant-change size: **220 lines**. Most of that is a better SQLite key/schema plus migration path, timestamp-aware upsert logic, parser hardening, expanded failure semantics, and tests for those cases.

Bottom line: **No, I would not approve this as-is**. It is a decent prototype, but the primary-key/upsert behavior is too risky for accounting data.

issues.description: job_id is the sole primary key, collapsing distinct duplicate/requeued/federated/resized Slurm accounting records.
Equal terminal state rank lets older terminal records overwrite newer terminal records based on ingest order.
Failure reports omit Slurm failure-like terminal states such as BOOT_FAIL, DEADLINE, NODE_FAIL, and PREEMPTED.
Elapsed parser is too narrow for some valid Slurm accounting time formats.
Database schema has no versioning or migration path for existing user databases.
Parser accepts empty user/partition and negative AllocCPUS values that corrupt reports.
Importer requires one exact header order and raw pipe splitting, making valid sacct format variations brittle.
Read-only report commands silently create an empty database when the db path is wrong.
Project lacks configured linting, typing, or static checks beyond pytest.
